text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

Thanks for reaching out, C. I'm here to help the three of you find a plan that addresses everyone's concerns, and I'll keep a running list so we all see the same thing.

Before any options, I want to understand what matters to you and why. Two questions:

1. You said you're not signing off on A buying the house with her husband at a "family discount." Let me try to put the concern behind that: what I hear is that you want any transfer of the house to feel fair to all three of you — not just to whoever is buying. Is that close to it? Tell me what I'm missing.

2. You mentioned B "could use some money too." What matters most to you there — that the house's value gets shared among the three of you, that B is looked after specifically, or something else?

Also: has anyone said anything about the will's actual terms yet? I can't make legal decisions or move money, but knowing what the document says helps me keep the list accurate.

Does that wording fit? I'll record it only if you say so.

Mostly. I want a fair financial share and won’t subsidize A’s discounted purchase. B should share in the value too, but I’m not deciding for her. I don’t know the will’s actual terms yet. You can record that.

Hello A — I'm facilitating between you, B and C about your father's house and will. My job is to get everyone's concerns on the table and find a plan that meets all of them; I don't decide anything, and I can't make legal decisions or move money.

I understand you and your husband would like to buy the house at a family discount. Before plans, I want the need behind it. What matters to you and why? For example: keeping the house in the family, the home itself being yours, keeping it affordable, timing, your dad's wishes, or something else.

Also, what would make this feel acceptable to your sisters, from where you sit?

I'll write what you tell me as a short entry, show you the wording, and record it only when you confirm it fits.

What matters is having a secure, independent home and being financially independent. Buying it with my husband feels like a way to do that. I’d want the arrangement to feel fair to B and C, but I don’t know what would feel acceptable to them; C hasn’t agreed. I’m not sure what price or discount would be fair yet.

Hello B — I'm facilitating between you, A and C about your father's house and will. I'm gathering what matters to each of you so we can find a plan that covers everyone's concerns. I don't decide anything and can't make legal decisions or move money.

C mentioned you could use some money. What matters most to you here, and why? For example: getting your share of the house's value sooner, having a say in what happens, being treated the same as your sisters, or something else entirely.

Also — does anyone have even a minor discomfort with anything raised so far? "Not sure yet" is a fine answer; I record concerns, not agreements to overcome.

I'll show you the wording I'd record and only keep it once you say it fits.

I suppose having my share of the house’s value available sooner would help me get a dance studio started. I’d be uncomfortable with anything being treated as settled before all three of us agree; I’m not sure about the details yet.

Thanks, C. Here's the wording I'd record for you — please confirm or correct:

1 (C) — Fair share: wants her fair share of the house's value, and not to be paying toward a discounted purchase for A.
2 (C) — B included: wants B to share in the value too, without deciding for her.

Does that fit? Say yes and I'll keep them; say what's off and I'll reword.

Three more things:
- Has anyone shown you the will's actual terms, or do you know who holds the document? I can't read it for you, but the family's plan has to respect it.
- A told me she doesn't yet know what price or discount would be fair, and that she wants it to feel fair to you and B.
- Does anyone have even a minor discomfort with anything raised so far? Small ones count — they're often where the real need is.

Once all three of you have confirmed your entries, I'll draft options that meet them all and bring them back for you to check.

DRAFT OPTIONS that aim to meet all six:
O1. Independent valuation; A buys at full appraised value, with C's and B's shares paid at closing. Meets 1,2,3,4,5,6 — depends on whether A and her husband can fund the full value.
O2. A buys below market, and the shortfall to C and B is made up from A's own side (less of other estate assets, or a payment to them at closing). Meets 1,2,5,6; the size of any discount has to be agreed, not assumed.
O3. No transfer yet: A lives there and pays market rent into a three-way pot until an agreed later date and valuation. Meets 1,2,4,6 and gives B income sooner rather than a lump sum — weaker on 5.
O4. Sell on the open market, split proceeds three ways; A uses her share toward a secure home elsewhere. Meets 1,2,4,5,6, but not 3's wish for this particular house.

Which of these feel workable to you, and which give you even a minor discomfort? A "no" tells me what to add, not what to argue with. Also, please each ask the executor or your father's lawyer for the will's terms — I can't obtain or interpret it.

O1 could work with an independent valuation and my share paid in full, subject to the will. O2 only if A covers the entire shortfall herself—my share can’t be discounted. O3 doesn’t work for me as an open-ended arrangement. O4 is a reasonable fallback. I’ll ask about the will.

Update after all three replies — nothing is settled; this is where the group's views land:

- Gate from B (6) and C: nothing settles before the will's terms are known and all three agree.
